records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb#remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) which destroys the association row directly, bypassing Group#remove/GroupUser callbacks like primary-group/title cleanup and derived counters
add_members splits usernames on ',' without stripping whitespace, so 'bob, alice' fails to find ' alice'; it also returns success even when no usernames match existing users (silent no-op)
records.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, it does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then `User.find_by_username(username)`. There is no `strip` on each username, so an input like "bob, alice" yields " alice" and will not match a real "alice" username. Also, when none of the split values match a user, the loop makes no changes and `group.save` will still succeed, returning `success_json`

records.issue_text: admin groups create action only reads name and visible but ignores alias_level sent by the client's asJSON(), so a newly created group always gets the default alias level, silently dropping the admin's selection
records.rationale: Client now POSTs `alias_level` when creating a group (`Discourse.Group#asJSON` includes `alias_level`, and `create()` sends it as `data: this.asJSON()`), but `Admin::GroupsController#create` only sets `group.name` and `group.visible` and never assigns `alias_level`. This means the admin’s selected alias level is silently dropped on create and the group gets the model default.
